summary: Iter 171 mobile parity + dark-mode sweep passed. Verified all 12 target screens on Expo web preview: dark mode toggle from Settings applies and every screen (Ask Wayly, Upload, AI Decode, Invoice detail, Pacing, Budget Alerts, Budget Scenarios, Reports, Carer Self-Check, Handover Pack, AT & HM, CHSP Tools, Letters, Care Plans) renders with the themed palette — no white-on-white / dark-on-dark blending observed. Copy parity all matches spec (Budget Alerts subtitle + empty-state hint + no web-app footnote; Budget Scenarios PageIntro eyebrow/title/description; Reports PageIntro + 8 report types picker; Carer Self-Check + Handover Pack + AT & HM + CHSP Tools + Letters + Care Plans PageIntro titles all match). No `$$` doubled dollar signs anywhere in scanned pages. Pace status label uses themed colors.sage / colors.gold (readable in both modes). Per-participant scoping in code paths is via participant_id query + apiFetch's X-Participant-Id header for /reports, /pacing, /budget-scenarios, /care-plans, /letters; verified activeId hook re-fetches on switch.
critical_code_review_comments: reports.tsx load() calls /reports without an explicit participant_id query param — relies on apiFetch injecting X-Participant-Id via ParticipantContext. If that header logic ever regresses, reports list would leak across participants. Consider mirroring the pacing/care-plans pattern and appending ?participant_id=${activeId} defensively.
handover-pack.tsx GET /cs1/handover-packs does not filter by participant_id in the URL either — same X-Participant-Id header dependency. Confirm backend enforces scoping.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (12/12 routes verified in dark + copy checks)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Dark-mode toggle testID = theme-dark on Settings. All target screens render themed colors correctly. Copy strings verified via document.body.innerText scans (no $$ doubles, no 'on the web app' / 'Manage alert rules on the web app' leftovers). If retesting per-participant isolation, use the header switcher (participant-switcher testIDs) and re-check /reports, /handover-packs, /letters — those two rely on X-Participant-Id header rather than URL query, worth a direct verification against the backend.
